subject: general
question: Hariprasad Chaurasia, an Indian flutist in the Hindustani classical tradition, was awarded with which of the following awards in 2000?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Padma Vibhushan**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 1984 he was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi (National Academy of Music, Dance, and Drama) award for his outstanding contribution to music.
 
• He received two of India's highest civilian honours, the Padma Bhushan (1992) and the Padma Vibhushan (2000)
 
• Here are some other awards that Chaurasia received:
 
 
• Sangeet Natak Akademi: 1984
 
• Konark Samman: 1992
 
• Padma Bhushan: 1992
 
• Yasha Bharati Samman: 1994
 
• Akshaya Samman: 2009
 
• Pune Pandit Award: 2008 
 
 
 
• Chaurasia was born in Prayagraj on July 1, 1938.
 
• He was a member of the maihar Senia gharana, a community of performers with a distinctive musical style.
 
• He learned from the famous flute player Bholanath Prasanna.
 
• He also formed a group called Shiv-Hari with Santoor player Shiv Kumar Sharma. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Padma Shri
 
 
• The fourth highest civilian award, given for "distinguished service".
 
• It was established in 1954 and is awarded to Indian citizens for their contributions in various fields.
 
• The award is shaped like a geometric pattern on a circle, with the words "Padma" and "Shri" inscribed above and below a lotus flower in the center. 
 
 
 
• Padma Vibhushan
 
 
• The second highest civilian award, given for "exceptional and distinguished service".
 
• It was established in 1954. 
 
 
 
• Padma Bhushan
 
 
• The third highest civilian award, given for "distinguished service of a high order".
 
• It was established in 1954. 
 
 
 
• Bharat Ratna
 
 
• The highest civilian award, given for exceptional service or performance in any field.
 
• The Prime Minister makes recommendations to the President of India for the Bharat Ratna award, and the number of awards given in a year is limited to three. 
 
• The Government of India awards these civilian awards on Republic Day, January 26, each year.
